M is the fixed message count, so the original event compares the decoder to a constant rather than to the transmitted message. A noiseless binary identity code with M=2 has original error 1/2 although its actual decoding error is zero; a constant decoder outputting M has original error zero. This logically invalidates the defined reliability criterion. Introduced U uniform on [M], specified X_t=f_t(U,Y^{t-1}) and conditional path law, and corrected the error to Pr[g(Y^n) ne U], preserving the count, costs, causal maps and capacity convention.
